newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE July coffee up almost 14 pct in frenzied AM.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE July coffee up almost 14 pct in frenzied AM.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures, extending the rally in world coffee, surged to 20-month highs by Thursday midsession on what traders said was frenzied roaster-led buying and market talk of origin defaults in the Far East.
"The situation is getting completely out of hand but there's nothing to stop the rally," said one trader. "With the frost season starting in Brazil from this weekend, nobody wants to be short."

London benchmark July scooped a whopping 13.8 percent or $138 on the day to finish midday at session's high of $2,570. It rose by 10 percent in the first few minutes of trading. At $2,570, prices were the highest since September 1995. Volume reached 9,1904 lots.

The frenzied buying, which followed a new advance in New York on Wednesday, gathered pace after a major roaster placed buying orders for 2,000 lots, mainly in July and September. Nestle declined to comment on traders' views that it was buying.
Sentiment was also boosted by what the traders said were rumours from the Far East that some origin sellers could default on their earlier cheaper-priced contracts in view of the surging prices.
New York's July arabica contract came within a striking distance of hitting the closely-watched $3.00 a lb level on Wednesday. It hit a high of $2.97 before settling at 295.55 cents.
London traders said arabicas could touch $3.00 on Thursday but were not certain if the market could close above that level.
London, which was relatively undervalued compared with New York, could draw further strength if New York propels much higher.
Traders were talking of arabicas hitting $4 or $5 if a frost were to hit Brazil this year, with the prospect just as dramatic a drop if it does not.
"Wait until the market turns and there will be blood on the street," one said.
The London Clearing House said it has increased intra-day margin calls of two deposits of $625 each from now for all short members.
